summary.text: This opportunity briefing explores combining sparse autoencoders and activation patching within large language models to elicit latent factual and reasoning knowledge that is not reflected in surface outputs. By integrating mechanistic interpretability tools with representation engineering, the framework locates knowledge-bearing representations and extracts hidden knowledge without modifying model weights. This approach addresses limitations in contrastive activation methods that struggle with complex multi-step reasoning.

target_user.text: The target users are software companies and security engineers developing generative artificial intelligence driven code fixing pipelines and automated vulnerability patching systems, as indicated by patent assignee categories and repository tooling.

jtbd.text: When deploying large language models in production environments, developers want to reliably extract and verify latent factual and reasoning knowledge that remains hidden in internal representations, so that they can detect deceptive alignment and ensure safe model behavior without relying solely on surface-level outputs.

value_prop.text: Unlike contrastive consistency search approaches that struggle with complex multi-step reasoning tasks, this combined framework unifies sparse autoencoder feature analysis and activation patching to achieve higher average elicitation accuracy and surface hidden knowledge even when surface outputs are incorrect or evasive.

riskiest_assumption.text: The riskiest assumption, driven by a low desirability axis score of 2.0 on a scale up to 5, is that enterprise development teams building security applications actually experience a painful, unsolved workflow bottleneck around eliciting hidden model knowledge that they are willing to pay for or adopt a specialized interpretability framework to solve.

mvp.text: To test the riskiest assumption regarding market demand, we will launch a demand landing page outlining the latent knowledge extraction framework and conduct problem interviews with target users, aiming for a proposed threshold of 15 sign-ups or positive interview commitments out of 30 developer conversations.
mvp.type: demand landing page and problem interviews

success_metric.text: Success is measured by securing at least a proposed threshold of 5 pilot commitments from enterprise development teams during problem interviews and achieving a proposed threshold of 25 percent visitor conversion on the landing page.

kill_criteria.text: The opportunity should be killed if fewer than a proposed threshold of 5 percent of interviewed security engineers express a workflow pain point related to hidden latent knowledge.
The opportunity should be killed if landing page visitor conversion falls below a proposed threshold of 2 percent after running traffic acquisition experiments.

open_source.use: Used to automate the interpretation of sparse autoencoder features extracted from large language model internal representations.
Used to measure the depth of model representations and analyze internal states via activation patching techniques.
Used as a software security benchmark environment to evaluate model behavior and patch generation tasks.

to_build.text: A unified three-stage pipeline orchestrating sparse autoencoder feature analysis, activation patching, and causal verification to elicit latent knowledge without altering model weights.
